mcp_server/markitdown.tagline: Turn any document into clean Markdown
mcp_server/markitdown.overview: MarkItDown is a lightweight Microsoft utility that converts files like Word, PowerPoint, Excel, PDFs, images, and HTML into clean Markdown text. Markdown is token-efficient and something LLMs read very well, so this is a fast way to feed documents into an AI without losing headings, lists, tables, and links. As an MCP server it lets your assistant convert files on demand.
capabilities: Converts PDF, Word, PowerPoint, and Excel files to structured Markdown
Extracts text from images via OCR and reads EXIF metadata
Transcribes speech from audio files
Handles HTML, CSV, JSON, XML, EPub, and ZIP archives
Preserves headings, lists, tables, and links in the output
useCases: Students preparing lecture slides or PDFs as clean text for an AI tutor
Anyone who needs to summarize or query an Office document with an LLM
Building a pipeline that ingests mixed file types into one text format
howTo: Install with pip install markitdown[all] (Python 3.10+ recommended in a virtual environment)
For the MCP server, install the markitdown-mcp package
Add the markitdown MCP server to your client config (e.g. Claude Desktop)
Ask your assistant to convert a local file path or URL to Markdown
Use the CLI directly with markitdown yourfile.pdf for a quick one-off

example.label: Convert a file from the command line

goodToKnow: It does I/O with your process's permissions, so sanitize inputs in untrusted environments.
Output is optimized for AI consumption, not high-fidelity human-facing document conversion.

mcp_server/firecrawl.tagline: Scrape and crawl the web for AI
mcp_server/firecrawl.overview: Firecrawl is a web scraping and crawling API built for AI use. It handles JavaScript-heavy, dynamic pages and returns clean Markdown or structured JSON instead of messy HTML, so your agent can read the web reliably. It is open source and also offered as a hosted service with an API key.
capabilities: Scrapes single pages into clean Markdown or structured JSON
Crawls an entire site and returns content from every reachable page
Handles JavaScript-rendered and dynamic content
Extracts structured data using a schema you define
Returns screenshots and other page outputs
useCases: Giving an AI agent live, readable web context for research
Building a RAG knowledge base from a documentation site
Monitoring or extracting structured data from many pages at scale
howTo: Sign up at firecrawl.dev and get an API key (or self-host the open-source version)
Add the Firecrawl MCP server to your client and set FIRECRAWL_API_KEY
Run via npx -y firecrawl-mcp in your MCP config
Ask your assistant to scrape a URL or crawl a site
Provide a JSON schema when you want structured extraction
goodToKnow: The hosted API is usage-priced; heavy crawling consumes credits, so test on small scopes first.
Respect target sites' terms of service and robots rules when scraping.

mcp_server/knowledge-graph-memory.overview: Knowledge Graph Memory is an official reference MCP server that stores facts as a knowledge graph of entities, relations, and observations. This lets an AI assistant remember details about you and your projects and recall them across separate conversations, instead of forgetting everything between sessions. It is a simple, local persistent memory layer.
capabilities: Stores facts as entities connected by relations
Adds observations to entities over time
Recalls remembered information in later conversations
Lets the assistant search and read its own memory graph
Persists the graph locally as a JSON file
useCases: Keeping an assistant aware of your preferences and ongoing projects
Building a personal assistant that remembers people and context
Maintaining continuity across many short chat sessions
howTo: Add the memory server to your MCP client config
Run it with npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-memory
Optionally set MEMORY_FILE_PATH to choose where the graph is stored
Tell the assistant to remember a fact, then start a new chat and ask about it
Inspect the JSON memory file to see what was stored
goodToKnow: Memory is only as good as what the assistant chooses to write; results vary by client.
The graph is stored in plain text locally, so treat it as you would any local data file.

mcp_server/filesystem.tagline: Let your assistant read and write local files
mcp_server/filesystem.overview: Filesystem is an official reference MCP server that gives an AI assistant controlled access to your local files. It can read, write, search, and manage files, but only inside directories you explicitly allow, which keeps it sandboxed. This is the standard way to let an assistant work directly with files on your machine.
capabilities: Reads and writes files within allowed directories
Lists directories and searches for files
Creates, moves, and deletes files and folders
Restricts all access to the directories you whitelist
Returns file metadata
useCases: Letting an assistant edit code or notes in a specific project folder
Organizing or batch-renaming files through natural language
Reading reference documents from a chosen directory
howTo: Add the filesystem server to your MCP client config
Pass the allowed directory paths as arguments after the package name
Run with npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem /path/to/allowed/dir
Restart your client so it picks up the server
Ask the assistant to list or edit files in that directory
goodToKnow: Only the directories you pass are accessible; choose them narrowly for safety.
Giving write access means the assistant can change or delete files, so scope it carefully.

mcp_server/sequential-thinking.tagline: Structured step-by-step reasoning for hard problems
mcp_server/sequential-thinking.overview: Sequential Thinking is an official reference MCP server that helps a model break a complex problem into a numbered series of reasoning steps. The model can branch, revise earlier steps, and adjust how many steps it needs as understanding grows. It is a thinking aid rather than a tool that touches your files or the web.
capabilities: Breaks a problem into explicit, ordered thought steps
Lets the model revise or correct earlier steps
Supports branching into alternative lines of reasoning
Adjusts the number of steps dynamically as the problem unfolds
Keeps the reasoning process visible and structured
useCases: Working through multi-step planning or design problems
Debugging logic where the path is not obvious upfront
Any task that benefits from deliberate, revisable reasoning
howTo: Add the sequential-thinking server to your MCP client config
Run it with npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-sequential-thinking
Restart your client to load the tool
Pose a hard problem and let the assistant use the thinking tool
Watch it lay out and revise numbered steps
goodToKnow: It structures reasoning but does not by itself make the model smarter or factually correct.
Best paired with tools that act on the world, since it only organizes thinking.

mcp_server/context7.tagline: Up-to-date library docs inside your coding AI
mcp_server/context7.overview: Context7 by Upstash pulls current, version-accurate documentation and code examples for libraries straight into your coding assistant. Models often answer with outdated or made-up APIs; Context7 fixes that by injecting real docs from the source so the suggested code matches the version you are actually using. You add it by ending a prompt with 'use context7'.
capabilities: Fetches up-to-date documentation for thousands of libraries
Provides version-specific API and code examples
Injects real source docs into the model's context on demand
Reduces hallucinated or outdated API suggestions
Works across many MCP-compatible coding clients
useCases: Coding against a fast-moving library and needing current APIs
Students learning a framework who want accurate examples
Avoiding deprecated methods the model learned from old data
howTo: Add the Context7 MCP server to your client config
Run it with npx -y @upstash/context7-mcp
Optionally add a free Context7 API key for higher limits
Append 'use context7' to your coding prompt
Let the assistant pull and use the matching docs

example.label: Prompt that triggers Context7
example.snippet: Create a Next.js 15 route handler that streams a response. use context7

goodToKnow: Coverage depends on the library being indexed; obscure packages may be missing.
A free API key raises rate limits for heavier use.

mcp_server/chrome-devtools-mcp.tagline: Drive and debug Chrome through DevTools
mcp_server/chrome-devtools-mcp.overview: Chrome DevTools MCP lets an AI assistant control a real Chrome browser through the DevTools protocol. It can navigate pages, inspect the DOM, run performance traces, and watch network requests, so the assistant can actually debug and measure a live site rather than guess. It is maintained by the Chrome DevTools team.
capabilities: Controls a live Chrome browser for automation
Runs performance traces and analyzes load behavior
Inspects the DOM and page state
Monitors network requests and responses
Helps reproduce and debug front-end issues
useCases: Diagnosing why a web page is slow or janky
Letting an assistant verify a UI change in a real browser
Capturing network or console issues during debugging
howTo: Make sure a recent Chrome and Node.js are installed
Add the server to your MCP client config
Run it with npx -y chrome-devtools-mcp@latest
Ask the assistant to open a URL and analyze it
Request a performance trace or network inspection
goodToKnow: It launches and controls a real browser, so it needs Chrome present on the machine.
Automating browsing can consume real resources; point it only at sites you intend to test.

mcp_server/chrome-devtools.tagline: Test site speed and debug via Chrome DevTools
mcp_server/chrome-devtools.overview: Chrome DevTools MCP connects your AI assistant to Chrome through the DevTools protocol so it can test website speed, debug pages, and analyze performance in a live browser. Instead of describing a bug, you let the assistant open the page and measure it directly. It is the same Chrome DevTools team integration, installed via the chrome-devtools-mcp package.
capabilities: Opens and controls Chrome for live debugging
Measures page load and performance
Inspects page elements and console output
Tracks network activity during a session
Helps confirm fixes in a real browser
useCases: Checking real load performance of a page you built
Debugging a rendering or console error hands-on
Verifying that a front-end change behaves correctly
howTo: Install a recent Chrome and Node.js
Add the chrome-devtools-mcp server to your MCP client
Run it with npx -y chrome-devtools-mcp
Ask the assistant to load a URL and profile it
Review the performance and network results it reports
goodToKnow: Requires Chrome installed locally since it drives a real browser.
Pin a version if you need reproducible behavior across machines.

mcp_server/playwright-browser-automation.tagline: Automate browsers for testing with Playwright
mcp_server/playwright-browser-automation.overview: Playwright MCP by Microsoft lets an AI assistant drive a web browser using Playwright, navigating pages, clicking, filling forms, and reading content. It uses the page's accessibility tree rather than screenshots, which makes it fast and reliable for automated testing and web tasks. Think of it as a modern alternative to Selenium controlled through natural language.
capabilities: Navigates pages and clicks, types, and fills forms
Reads page content via the accessibility tree
Runs across Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit
Captures snapshots and screenshots when needed
Automates repeatable web workflows for testing
useCases: Writing or running automated end-to-end UI tests
Automating a repetitive web task like form submission
Letting an assistant verify a web flow step by step
howTo: Ensure Node.js is installed
Add the Playwright MCP server to your client config
Run it with npx -y @playwright/mcp
Ask the assistant to open a site and perform actions
Have it report the page state or test results
goodToKnow: It uses the accessibility tree by default, which is faster but differs from pixel-based tools.
Browser binaries may download on first run, so the first launch can be slower.

mcp_server/task-master.tagline: AI task management for coding projects
mcp_server/task-master.overview: Task Master is an AI-driven task management system that turns a project plan or PRD into a structured, trackable list of tasks and subtasks. It plugs into coding agents like Claude and Cursor through MCP, so your assistant can see what to do next and work through tasks in order. It brings agile-style organization to AI-assisted development.
capabilities: Parses a requirements doc into discrete tasks
Breaks tasks into subtasks with dependencies
Tracks task status and what to work on next
Integrates with coding agents over MCP
Keeps the project plan and the agent in sync
useCases: Managing a larger coding project with an AI pair programmer
Turning a spec into an ordered, trackable backlog
Keeping an agent focused on one task at a time
howTo: Add the task-master MCP server to your client config
Run it with npx -y task-master-ai
Provide API keys for the model provider you want it to use
Initialize a project and parse a PRD into tasks
Ask the assistant for the next task and work through them
goodToKnow: It needs model API keys configured to generate and expand tasks.
Quality of the task breakdown depends on how clear your input spec is.

mcp_server/repomix.tagline: Pack a whole codebase into one AI file
mcp_server/repomix.overview: Repomix packs an entire repository into a single, AI-friendly file so you can hand a whole codebase to an LLM at once. It can compress the output, respect .gitignore, and strip secrets before sharing. As an MCP server it lets your assistant package a repo on demand for analysis or review.
capabilities: Bundles a full repo into one structured file
Compresses output to fit more code in context
Respects .gitignore and custom ignore rules
Removes detected secrets before output
Reports token counts for the packed result
useCases: Asking an AI to review or explain an entire project
Onboarding to an unfamiliar codebase quickly
Preparing a repo as context for a code audit
howTo: Ensure Node.js is installed
Run npx -y repomix in your project to produce a packed file
Or add the repomix MCP server to your client config
Ask the assistant to pack the repo and analyze it
Use the security check option to scrub secrets before sharing
goodToKnow: Very large repos can still exceed model context limits even after compression.
Always review the output before sharing; secret removal is a safeguard, not a guarantee.

mcp_server/serena.tagline: Semantic, IDE-grade code tools for agents
mcp_server/serena.overview: Serena is a free, open-source coding toolkit that gives an LLM IDE-like abilities such as semantic code retrieval, editing, and refactoring at the symbol level. Instead of working with raw line numbers or plain text search, your agent understands the code's structure, which makes it faster and more reliable on large codebases. It connects to any MCP client.
capabilities: Finds and navigates code by symbols, not just text
Performs semantic edits and refactors like renames and moves
Looks up references across files
Works language-agnostically via language servers
Connects to any LLM through MCP
useCases: Refactoring safely across a large or complex codebase
Helping an agent navigate unfamiliar code precisely
Cross-file renames and reference lookups without manual hunting
howTo: Install uv (the Python package manager) first
Run the server via uvx --from git+https://github.com/oraios/serena serena start-mcp-server
Add that command to your MCP client config
Point Serena at your project directory
Ask the agent to navigate or refactor using its semantic tools
goodToKnow: The maintainers warn against installing via marketplaces, which ship outdated commands; follow the official quick start.
It relies on language servers, so very niche languages may have weaker support.

mcp_server/mastra-docs.tagline: Mastra framework docs inside your assistant
mcp_server/mastra-docs.overview: Mastra Docs is an MCP server that gives an AI assistant direct access to the full documentation for Mastra.ai, the TypeScript agent framework. When you are building with Mastra, your assistant can answer questions and generate code grounded in the current official docs and examples instead of guessing. It is the fastest way to keep an assistant accurate about Mastra.
capabilities: Serves Mastra's full documentation to the assistant
Provides current code examples for the framework
Answers framework-specific questions accurately
Reduces outdated or invented Mastra APIs
Runs locally via a simple npx command
useCases: Building an agent or workflow with the Mastra framework
Learning Mastra with accurate, up-to-date guidance
Avoiding hallucinated APIs while coding against Mastra
howTo: Ensure Node.js is installed
Add the Mastra docs server to your MCP client config
Run it with npx -y @mastra/mcp-docs-server
Restart your client to load it
Ask Mastra questions and let it pull from the docs
goodToKnow: It is specific to the Mastra framework and not a general documentation tool.
Most useful when you are actually building with Mastra.

mcp_server/beads.tagline: Persistent issue memory for coding agents
mcp_server/beads.overview: Beads is a lightweight issue-tracking memory layer that gives a coding agent persistent context across a project. Instead of losing track of work between sessions, the agent records and reads issues like a graph of tasks, so it stays oriented and works more reliably over time. It runs as an MCP server alongside your agent.
capabilities: Stores work as persistent, linked issues
Lets the agent recall context across sessions
Tracks dependencies between pieces of work
Keeps the agent oriented on long-running projects
Runs locally as an MCP server
useCases: Long-running coding projects where context keeps getting lost
Helping an agent remember outstanding work between sessions
Tracking dependent tasks an agent is working through
howTo: Install the `bd` CLI: `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gastownhall/beads/main/scripts/install.sh | bash`
Run `bd init` once inside your project to set up the issue store
Point your MCP client (Claude Code, Cursor, etc.) at the beads MCP server
Let the agent create and read issues as it works
Resume a later session and have it recall prior context
goodToKnow: It is a memory and tracking aid; the agent still has to choose to use it well.
Best value shows up on multi-session projects, less so for quick one-offs.

mcp_server/blender.tagline: Build 3D scenes in Blender by prompting
mcp_server/blender.overview: BlenderMCP connects Blender to an AI assistant through the Model Context Protocol, letting you create and edit 3D scenes with natural language. The assistant can add and modify objects, apply materials, inspect the scene, and even download assets, all by talking to a small server running inside Blender. It makes prompt-assisted 3D modeling possible.
capabilities: Creates, modifies, and deletes 3D objects in a scene
Applies and edits materials and colors
Inspects the scene and views the viewport
Searches and downloads assets (Sketchfab, Poly Haven)
Runs Python code inside Blender from the assistant
useCases: Beginners building simple 3D scenes without learning Blender's UI first
Quickly prototyping or arranging a scene by description
Pulling in ready-made assets while modeling
howTo: Install Blender 3.0+ and the uv package manager
Download addon.py from the repo and enable it in Blender's add-ons
Add the blender-mcp server to your client (uvx blender-mcp or npx -y blender-mcp)
Start the server inside Blender's BlenderMCP panel
Ask the assistant to create or modify objects in the scene
goodToKnow: It can run arbitrary Python inside Blender, so only use it with trusted prompts and save your work first.
It sends anonymous telemetry about which tools run, which you can review in the docs.

mcp_server/oh-my-posh.tagline: Validate your Oh My Posh prompt theme
mcp_server/oh-my-posh.overview: This Oh My Posh MCP server checks your prompt theme configuration against the official schema so you catch mistakes before they break your terminal prompt. Oh My Posh is a cross-shell prompt theme engine, and a small typo in its config can silently misbehave; this validates it for you. It is a focused helper rather than a broad automation tool.
capabilities: Validates Oh My Posh theme configs against the official schema
Catches structural errors before they break the prompt
Explains what is wrong in a config
Works with JSON, YAML, or TOML theme files
Helps you author valid custom prompts faster
useCases: Building or editing a custom Oh My Posh prompt theme
Debugging a prompt config that is not rendering right
Confirming a downloaded theme is schema-valid before using it
howTo: Install Oh My Posh if you have not already
Add this MCP server to your client config
Point it at your theme configuration file
Ask the assistant to validate the config
Fix any errors it reports and re-validate
goodToKnow: It validates configuration; it does not design a theme for you.
A valid config can still look wrong visually, so preview the prompt too.

mcp_server/stripe.tagline: Run Stripe payments and billing from Claude
mcp_server/stripe.overview: The Stripe MCP server lets Claude work directly with your Stripe account to view payments data and run billing and payment workflows. You can ask about customers, charges, invoices, and subscriptions in plain language, and have the assistant perform supported Stripe operations. It connects through your Stripe API key.
capabilities: Looks up customers, charges, and payment data
Manages invoices and subscriptions where supported
Runs billing and payment workflows by request
Answers questions about your Stripe account in plain English
Connects securely via your Stripe API key
useCases: Checking recent payments or a customer's billing status
Automating routine billing tasks through conversation
Pulling Stripe data without writing API code yourself
howTo: Get a Stripe API key from your Stripe dashboard
Add the Stripe MCP server to your Claude client config
Provide the API key as the configured credential
Restart your client to load the connector
Ask Claude to look up or act on your Stripe data

example.label: Ask Claude about Stripe data
example.snippet: Show me my 10 most recent successful charges in Stripe.

goodToKnow: Use a restricted or test-mode key first, since this touches real billing data and actions.
Available actions depend on the scopes your API key grants.

mcp_server/clay.tagline: Enrich leads and run GTM workflows in Clay
mcp_server/clay.overview: The Clay MCP server connects Claude to Clay so it can enrich data and run go-to-market and prospecting workflows. You can ask the assistant to look up and enrich contacts or companies and drive your Clay tables through conversation. It connects through your Clay account credentials.
capabilities: Enriches contact and company data via Clay
Runs prospecting and go-to-market workflows
Works with your Clay tables and data
Answers questions about enriched records
Connects through your Clay account
useCases: Sales and growth users enriching a list of leads
Automating prospecting research through conversation
Driving Clay GTM workflows without manual clicking
howTo: Have an active Clay account with the data you want to use
Add the Clay MCP server to your Claude client config
Provide your Clay credentials as configured
Restart your client to load the connector
Ask Claude to enrich a contact or run a workflow

example.label: Ask Claude to enrich a lead
example.snippet: Enrich this person in Clay: jane@example.com and summarize their company.

goodToKnow: Enrichment can consume Clay credits depending on your plan.
Available actions depend on your Clay account permissions and connected sources.

mcp_server/github.tagline: Work with GitHub repos, issues, and PRs
mcp_server/github.overview: The GitHub MCP server lets Claude work with your GitHub repositories, issues, and pull requests. You can browse code, search a repo, read and create issues, and review or comment on pull requests through conversation. It connects using a GitHub access token scoped to what you allow.
capabilities: Browses and searches repository code
Reads, creates, and comments on issues
Views and reviews pull requests
Looks up repository details and history
Connects via a scoped GitHub access token
useCases: Triaging issues or summarizing a repo without leaving chat
Reviewing a pull request with AI help
Searching code across a project conversationally
howTo: Create a GitHub personal access token with the scopes you need
Add the GitHub MCP server to your Claude client config
Provide the token as the configured credential
Restart your client to load the connector
Ask Claude to read an issue, search code, or review a PR

example.label: Ask Claude about a repo
example.snippet: Summarize the open issues labeled 'bug' in my-org/my-repo.

goodToKnow: Scope the token to least privilege; write access lets the assistant change issues and PRs.
Available actions depend on the token's permissions and repo access.

mcp_server/microsoft-365.tagline: Connect Claude to your Microsoft 365 apps
mcp_server/microsoft-365.overview: The Microsoft 365 MCP server connects Claude to Microsoft 365 so it can read data and run actions across apps like Outlook, Teams, and OneDrive. You can ask about emails, calendar events, files, and more, and have the assistant act on them through conversation. It connects through your Microsoft 365 account sign-in.
capabilities: Reads email, calendar, and file data across Microsoft 365
Runs supported actions in apps like Outlook and Teams
Searches your documents and messages
Surfaces calendar and contact information
Connects through your Microsoft 365 account
useCases: Summarizing recent email or your day's calendar
Finding a document across OneDrive or SharePoint
Automating routine Microsoft 365 tasks conversationally
howTo: Add the Microsoft 365 MCP server to your Claude client config
Sign in and authorize access to your Microsoft 365 account
Grant the permissions the connector requests
Restart your client to load the connector
Ask Claude to read or act on your Microsoft 365 data

example.label: Ask Claude about your inbox
example.snippet: Summarize my unread Outlook emails from today and flag anything urgent.

goodToKnow: Access scope depends on the permissions you grant and your organization's policies.
An admin may need to approve the connector in managed Microsoft 365 tenants.
